These are lists of things you should also do to make life better for us all. Each page follows the same pattern: the claim, the alternatives, who is responsible, what we need them to do, and whether they have done it yet.

Everyday things

  • Smart MetersGet rid of your Smart meter. They're not Smart…
  • BroadbandStop paying for a fixed broadband line you don't need.
  • ToothpasteRead the ingredients on the label.
  • Cooking OilsRead the label. Check the claim.
  • Location on Your PhoneSwitch it off when you do not need it.
  • SupermarketsKnow who you are actually paying.
  • Credit ScoresCheck the file behind the score.
  • QR CodesLook at what a code actually asks for.
  • Amalgam FillingsAsk your dentist about the options.
  • Cash vs CardUnderstand what each one costs you.
  • Soya MilkCheck the ingredients and the nutrition label.
  • The BBCCompare the output, then decide.

Taking action

None of the above gets fixed by complaining alone. It gets fixed by people taking practical action together — and small groups can do that far more effectively than one person trying to change a system alone.

The internet is the tool that makes this possible now in a way it was not before. You do not need a large organisation. You need a handful of people who agree on one specific change and will keep at it.

Show you're in Send us something

How to read these pages. The "claim" section explains the issue as it stands, including where the popular version of the story is exaggerated or wrong. The "have they done it yet?" section answers honestly — sometimes partly, sometimes not at all.
